subject: Post-demo handoff: API credentialing, service accounts, and integration checklist
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Charlie Ng <charlie@acme.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 09 Mar 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo handoff: API credentialing, service accounts, and integration checklist

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today — appreciate the concise agenda and the live example you showed of the inference pipeline. As promised, here’s a short recap focused on the auth + integration items we agreed to cover next.

High-level items we’ll help ACME with:
- SDK quickstart and sample app to validate token exchange and streaming (we'll provide Node and Python examples)
- Authentication options: API keys (short-lived), OAuth2/JWT for user-bound flows, and service account short-lived tokens for server-to-server
- Key rotation: recommend automated rotation at 30/90 day cadence depending on key type; we can provide rotation scripts for GCP/AWS
- Routing & regional considerations: production traffic should be pinned to us-west-2 initially; failover policy to us-east-1 mapped in the MAP
- Structured output/tool-calls: outline mapping for tool-calling hooks and a list of recommended embeddings/reranker candidates

Immediate asks from ACME (from the call):
1) Confirm preferred auth pattern for internal batch jobs vs customer-facing features (you flagged service accounts for batch).
2) Provide sample IP allowlist template so your infra can open egress to Redwood endpoints.
3) Share SOC2 front-door evidence request list for the security team.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf (sample code), acme-ip-allowlist-template.csv, mutual_action_plan_ACME.xlsx (draft MAP)

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll share the MAP draft and SDK quickstart by EOD Monday.
- Ben, can you sketch a short rotation script for GCP service accounts we can attach to the MAP?
- Marissa, can you own scheduling a 30-min follow-up with ACME SecOps to walk the template?

Thanks — Jordan

Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0142
From: Charlie Ng <charlie@acme.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Kumar <sanjay.kumar@acme.io>, ACME Security Team <security@acme.io>
Date: Mon, 10 Mar 2025 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo handoff: API credentialing, service accounts, and integration checklist

Jordan — really helpful recap, thank you. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- For internal batch processing (nightly scoring), we prefer short-lived service-account tokens with 1-hour lifetime and automated rotation.
- For the customer-facing integration, we need an option for OAuth/JWT so customers can bind their accounts without exposing long-lived API keys.
- Security team asked for the SOC2 evidence list and the IP allowlist template.

We are happy to run the Node sample against our staging environment early next week. Can you include a short note on how the SDK handles prefix caching and KV cache behavior (we want to ensure predictable latency for scoring pipelines)?

Charlie
Principal Engineer, Integrations — ACME
charlie@acme.io
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Mar 2025 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo handoff: API credentialing, service accounts, and integration checklist

Jordan — putting together the rotation script now. Notes for the MAP and snippets I’ll attach:
- GCP service account flow: create short-lived OAuth2 token via IAM SignBlob -> exchange with Redwood token endpoint. I’ll include a bash + Python snippet and a Terraform pattern for IAM bindings.
- If ACME wants to avoid a persistent key, we recommend workload identity federation (WI Federation) to mint short-lived credentials instead of storing SA keys.
- For API keys used by internal SRE dashboards, we can enable per-key usage limits and automatic 30-day rotation with an audit webhook to ACME’s logging endpoint.

I’ll drop the files into the Drive link Jordan shared and attach to the MAP.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Charlie Ng <charlie@acme.io>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Mar 2025 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo handoff: API credentialing, service accounts, and integration checklist

Charlie / Sanjay — I pulled together a draft mutual action plan with milestones and owners (attached). Key dates I propose:
- 2025-03-13: ACME runs Node quickstart in staging (validation)
- 2025-03-16: SecOps sync to review SOC2 evidence and IP allowlist (30 minutes)
- 2025-03-20: Confirm routing & failover config, finalize region pinning
- 2025-03-25: Production cutover window (tentative)

I also added a checklist entry for structured outputs: we’ll provide a sample JSON schema for tool-calling responses and a small reranker evaluation set (5 queries) for ACME to try.

Please let me know if the dates look tight and I’ll push them. I’ve attached the MAP and a short runbook for onboarding the service account exchange.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Charlie Ng <charlie@acme.io>, Sanjay Kumar <sanjay.kumar@acme.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Mar 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo handoff: API credentialing, service accounts, and integration checklist

All — thanks for the quick turnaround. Confirming next actions: 
1) Ben will upload rotation snippets and the Terraform example to the Drive link by EOD today.
2) Jordan/Marissa will send the SDK quickstart and the structured-output JSON schema Monday morning.
3) Charlie/Sanjay: please confirm a 30-minute SecOps slot on 2025-03-16 or propose an alternative.

If ACME wants, we can flip the staging Node sample to use WI Federation instead of a keyed SA to demonstrate the no-key flow. That might reduce audit friction.

Thanks — looking forward to the SecOps sync.

Jordan

--- Forwarded attachment stubs ---
1) redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)
2) acme-ip-allowlist-template.csv (CSV)
3) mutual_action_plan_ACME.xlsx (Excel)
